_about: LTEC's quick checks (issue #37): standard first-pass tests of a deal, computed from each case's own numbers by quick_checks (core.py) = quickChecks (core.js). Each check reads one metric (over the whole hold: its worst year, or year 1) and rates it green / amber / red against the thresholds here. These are house rules of thumb for multifamily, not lender or legal requirements; a deal can override a threshold in its deal file (deal.json 'screens': {id: {green, amber, source}}), e.g. its loan's actual covenant. Edit this file and every deal follows.

checks.label: Debt-service coverage (DSCR)
checks.why: NOI ÷ debt service. Lenders typically require 1.20–1.25× or more; below 1.0× the property doesn't cover its loan payments.

checks.label: Debt yield
checks.why: Year-1 NOI ÷ the loan. Lenders typically look for 8–10%: it's their return if they had to take the property.

checks.label: Breakeven: share of rent needed
checks.why: Operating costs, debt service, reserves and the AM fee, less other income, as a share of the rent the case collects. The rest is the cushion: how far rent can fall before cash flow after debt hits zero.

checks.label: Exit cap vs going-in cap
checks.why: Exit cap rate minus the going-in cap rate. Below zero, the sale assumes the market pays more per dollar of NOI than we did: value growth from the market alone, a common optimistic assumption.

checks.label: Loan-to-value at purchase
checks.why: Loan ÷ purchase price. More leverage lifts returns and the risk that a dip in value wipes out the equity.

checks.label: Expense ratio
checks.why: Year-1 operating expenses ÷ income. Multifamily typically runs 35–50%; well below that often means a budget missing items (taxes reset at sale, insurance, payroll).

checks.label: Other income share
checks.why: Other income (fees, RUBS, parking…) ÷ total income in year 1. A large share is less certain than rent.
